Why the plural/singular split: the plural 'iyyim is 'islands' in Isaiah 40–66 and Ezekiel; the singular 'i in Isaiah 13–23 is 'coastland', a place on the sea's edge (Tyre, Philistia), so one English per Hebrew form.

a Friend (capitalized as a title: 'one of the king's Friends')

ἀνάστασις / ἀνίστημι, of the dead (2 Maccabees 7:9, 14; 12:43–44)
resurrection / raise (never 'rise up' alone for the rising of the dead)
the days of keeping apart (the persecution years, when faithful Jews refused to mix with Gentile ways; the Latin and the KJV at 14:3 reverse it to 'mingling')
wisdom; 'Wisdom' with a capital where she is personified (chiefly 6–10); τεχνῖτις σοφία (14:2) 'a craftsman's wisdom'

spirit (capital S only for God's Spirit, 1:7; 9:17, by context, with a note; 12:1 'your imperishable spirit'); 'breath' where it is the life-breath (2:3; 11:20 'one breath'; 15:11, 16; 16:14); 'wind' at 13:2 and 17:18
λόγος / ῥῆμα, God's; λογισμός (Wisdom of Solomon 9:1; 12:9; 16:12, 26; 18:15, 22)

word (lowercase, even at 18:15 'your all-powerful word', with a note there on John 1:1 and the Christian reading of the Logos; ῥῆμα 16:26 'word' too) / λογισμός 'reasoning' (plural 'reasonings, thoughts')
soul (the Greek sense matters in this book; 16:9 and 16:14 included; a note where 'life' is the sense, e.g. 15:8)
righteous (the righteous, a righteous person) / unrighteous / righteousness (1:1, 15)
ἀφθαρσία / ἄφθαρτος / φθαρτός / φθορά (Wisdom of Solomon)
incorruption / imperishable / perishable / decay (moral 'corruption' by context, 14:12, 25); note at first use in each part
holy ones (ὅσιοι 'your holy ones'; ἅγιοι 18:9 'the saints' would mislead, so 'the holy people', with a note)
Δέσποτα / δεσπότης, of God (Wisdom of Solomon)
παιδεύω / νουθετέω / κολάζω / κόλασις (Wisdom of Solomon)
idol / carved image / object of worship
commander (as John 18:12; gloss or note at first use: a Roman tribune, 'commander of a thousand'); σπεῖρα 'cohort'; ἑκατοντάρχης / ἑκατόνταρχος 'centurion'
barracks (the Antonia fortress; gloss at first use); in Hebrews 13:11, 13 and Revelation 20:9 'camp'
the Sanhedrin (as Matthew 5:22; 26:59), the Jewish high council; topic sanhedrin
the Hellenists / the Hebrews (gloss at first use: Greek-speaking and Aramaic-speaking Jews; note at Acts 6:1 on the readings)
the commander of the temple (as Acts 4:1; gloss: the priest in charge of the temple police); his ὑπηρέται 'guards' (as John 7:32; 18:3)
Founder (as Acts 3:15 'the Founder of life'; 5:31 'Founder and Savior'), with a note on 'leader, prince, pioneer'
builder (a craftsman in wood and stone; note at first use that the traditional English is 'carpenter'); Matthew 13:55 'the builder's son', Mark 6:3 'the builder'
John the Baptist (the noun, Matthew; Mark 6:25; 8:28) / John the Baptizer (Mark's participle, 1:4; 6:14, 24), so the reader can see Mark's variation
synagogue leader (gloss at first use: a local leader who ran the meetings)
act of power / acts of power (as Matthew 11:20–23; 13:54, 58; Mark 6:2, 5); gloss 'miracles'

overseer (note at first use in each book: the word behind English 'bishop'; in Acts 20:17, 28 and Titus 1:5–7 the same leaders are called elders); πρεσβύτεροι of church leaders 'elders'; ἐπισκοπή is 'charge' or 'office' where it means a position, not a person (Acts 1:20 'his charge')

judgment seat in Acts and Paul's letters (gloss or note at first use: the raised platform where a Roman official heard cases); exception Acts 12:21 'platform', where Herod speaks from it; in Acts 7:5 'a foot of ground'. Matthew 27:19 'the judge's bench' and John 19:13 'the judge's platform' were published before this entry and are not governed by it; the lead may align them at publish.
proconsul (gloss at first use: the Roman governor of a senatorial province)
οἱ φοβούμενοι τὸν θεόν / οἱ σεβόμενοι (τὸν θεόν) / προσήλυτος (Acts 10:2, 22; 13:16, 26, 43, 50; 16:14; 17:4, 17; 18:7)

those who fear God / those who worship God (Gentile sympathizers of the synagogue; gloss at first use in each part: 'non-Jews who worship Israel's God') / proselyte (a full convert to Judaism; gloss 'convert to Judaism'); note at 13:16 on the God-fearers debate
common / unclean (both kept, as the Acts brief fixes for Peter's vision: 'What God has made clean, you must not call common'); κοινόω 'call common' or 'make common' by context
Christian (in quotation marks at Acts 11:26, where the name is new; note there on the Latin-style ending and who coined it)

alms / give alms (as Acts 3:2–3 and the Septuagint term for Tobit; 10:2 'He gave much in alms to the people'); gloss at first use in each part 'gifts to the poor'. Matthew 6:2–4 renders the phrase 'give to the poor', which stays as it is

tongues (of fire, Acts 2:3) / speak in tongues (the gift: Acts 10:46; 19:6; 1 Corinthians 12–14), with a gloss and the topic spiritual-gifts; but 'speak in other languages' at Acts 2:4 and 'our own languages' at 2:11, where Luke says the hearers understood them in their native languages (διάλεκτος 'native language', 2:6, 8); the 2:4 note gives the shared word
the Nazarene ('Jesus the Nazarene', as Matthew 26:71 and John 18:5; 'Jesus Christ the Nazarene', Acts 3:6; 4:10); Ναζαρηνός (Mark) also 'the Nazarene'; 'the sect of the Nazarenes' (Acts 24:5)
παῖς, of Jesus and of David (Acts 3:13, 26; 4:25, 27, 30; Matthew 12:18)
servant ('his servant Jesus', 'your holy servant Jesus', 'your servant David'), with a note at Acts 3:13 on Isaiah 52:13 and the KJV's 'Son' or 'child'
δεσπότης / Δέσποτα, of God (Luke 2:29; Acts 4:24; Revelation 6:10)

Master (as for God in Judith, 2 Maccabees and Wisdom); of Christ in Jude 1:4 and 2 Peter 2:1 as there; distinct from ἐπιστάτης, also 'Master' (Luke's word for Jesus as the disciples' leader); glosses name the Greek word where both occur
ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτό, of the believers (Acts 1:15; 2:1, 44, 47; 1 Corinthians 11:20; 14:23)
together / in one place / in the same place by context; Acts 2:47 'to the gathering' (the Byzantine 'to the church' is a variant)

freedom of speech / freely / speak freely (Acts 2:29 'speak freely'; 4:13 'speak so freely'); where danger is present, pair freedom with courage rather than 'boldness' alone (4:29 'with complete freedom and courage'; 4:31 'freely and fearlessly'); 'boldly' may stand for παρρησιάζομαι in narrative (9:27–28); 28:31 'with complete freedom to speak'; note at Acts 4:13
your holy one (lowercase; the Greek of the Psalm), with a note that the site's Psalm 16:10, from the Hebrew chasid, reads 'your loyal one'

Master (Luke's own word for Jesus, used where Mark has 'Rabbi' or 'Teacher'; distinct from δεσπότης 'Master', said of God at Luke 2:29 and Acts 4:24, so a gloss at first use, Luke 5:5, names the Greek word, and the note there explains the difference)
lake (Luke's word for the Lake of Galilee, where Matthew and Mark say 'sea'; Luke 5:1 'Lake Gennesaret')

lawyer / the lawyers (experts in the Law of Moses, Luke's usual word where Mark and Matthew say 'scribes'; gloss at first use in each part: 'experts in the Law of Moses, not courtroom lawyers'); kept distinct from γραμματεῖς 'scribes'. Titus 3:13 (Zenas the νομικός) is left out: he may have been a Torah expert or a Roman jurist

sanctuary (ναός, the holy building itself, which only priests entered: Matthew 27:51; Mark 15:38; Luke 1:9, 21–22) / temple (ἱερόν, the whole complex with its courts, where crowds gathered and Jesus taught: Luke 2:27, 46; 19:45–47) in Matthew, Mark, Luke and Acts; note at first use in each book. John keeps its own published decision: ἱερόν 'temple grounds', ναός 'temple' (John 2:14–21). Pagan ναοί are 'shrines' (Acts 17:24). 2 Maccabees keeps 'temple' for both. Lowercase 'temple' in all prose. Why: already the practice in Matthew and Mark, and Luke and Acts keep it; John was published first, and its wordplay at 2:19–21 ('Tear this temple down ... the temple of his body') reads naturally only with 'temple', so John's notes explain the Greek there instead.

wealth (as Matthew 6:24; note at first use in each book: Aramaic mamona, 'wealth, property', the KJV's 'mammon', not the name of a demon); Luke 16:9, 11 μαμωνᾶς τῆς ἀδικίας / ὁ ἄδικος μαμωνᾶς 'the wealth of dishonesty' / 'dishonest wealth'
κόλπος, of reclining at a meal (John 1:18; 13:23; Luke 16:22–23)
embrace (as John 1:18 'the Father's embrace' and John 13:23; Luke 16:22 'Abraham's embrace', with a gloss on the place of honor at a feast; KJV 'bosom', other versions 'side')

sensible (good sense: Matthew 7:24; 24:45; 25:2; Luke 12:42 'faithful and sensible'); shrewd / shrewdly where it means worldly cleverness (Luke 16:8, with a note linking 12:42); Matthew 10:16 'sharp' (snakes)

dod, the man in the woman's mouth: my lover (never 'beloved'); dodim: lovemaking (1:2, 4; 4:10; 5:1; 7:12) with a note at 1:2 that the Greek and Latin read dadayim, 'breasts' (variant at 1:2, 1:4, 4:10); 5:1 'be drunk with lovemaking' with the vocative 'lovers' in a variant
ra'yah / re'a / re'im / chaverim (Song of Songs)
ra'yah (his word for her): my darling; re'a (5:16): friend; re'im (5:1): friends; chaverim (1:7; 8:13): companions

love, every time (never 'desire' or 'lust'); the refrain at 2:7, 3:5 and 8:4 is one English line each time: 'I make you swear, daughters of Jerusalem, ... do not wake love and do not stir it up / until it wants to' (8:4 lacks the gazelles; mah for im noted at 8:4); 'love has made me sick' at 2:5 and 5:8
bnot Yerushalayim / bnot Tsiyyon / hashulammit (Song of Songs 3:11; 6:13)
the daughters of Jerusalem / the daughters of Zion (3:11, with a 4QCant-a variant) / the Shulammite (note at 6:13 on Shunem, Abishag and Shelomoh)
bride / my sister: 'my sister, my bride' (a lovers' word, as in Egyptian love songs, not a blood tie; note at 4:9); 8:8 'our sister' is a family relation
nerd / mor / kofer / karkom / qaneh / qinnamon / levonah / ahalot / besamim / pardes (Song of Songs 1:12–14; 4:6, 13–14)
nard / myrrh / henna / saffron / calamus / cinnamon / frankincense / aloes / spices / orchard (pardes, a Persian word: note at 4:13); one spice is one English word across the book
shoshannah / chavatselet hasharon / tappuach (Song of Songs 2:1–5; 7:8; 8:5)
lily / a crocus of the Sharon plain (note on the 'rose of Sharon' at 2:1: the woman speaks, not Christ) / apple tree, apples (note: the fruit may be apricot or quince)
gazelle / young deer / fawns; 'gazelles or does of the field' (tseva'ot / ayyelot hassadeh) at 2:7 and 3:5 with a note on the wordplay with tseva'ot, 'armies', and El Shaddai
shalhevetyah / reshef / qin'ah / 'az kammavet ahavah (Song of Songs 8:6)

a flame of Yah (superlative reading in the note and the views) / sparks (of fire; the Hebrew reshef can also mean flashes or plague-bolts) / jealousy (the word covers fierce loyalty and is used of God) / love is strong, like death; Sheol with a gloss at first use
shadayim / beten / shorer / yarekh / yad / me'ay / gan / kerem / peri (Song of Songs)

breasts / belly / navel (alternatives in the note at 7:2) / thigh / hand (5:4) / insides (5:4; 'me'av' 5:14 'belly') / garden / vineyard / fruit; no euphemism is added or removed, and each is explained in a note
the one I love with my whole self (3:1–4 and 1:7, the same phrase each time); 5:6 'my life went out of me'; 6:12 'my longing'
dodi li va'ani lo (Song of Songs 2:16; 6:3; 7:10)

'My lover belongs to me, and I belong to him' (2:16); 'I belong to my lover, and my lover belongs to me' (6:3); 'I belong to my lover, and his desire is toward me' (7:10); the Hebrew order changes each time (note at 2:16)
until the day breathes and the shadows run away (the same line both times; note at 2:17 on dawn or evening)
Tirtsah / Amanah / Senir / Hermon / Heshbon / Bat-rabbim / Baal-hamon / Kedar / En-gedi (Song of Songs)
Tirzah / Amana / Senir / Hermon / Heshbon / Bat-rabbim / Baal-hamon / Kedar / En-gedi; Lebanon is 'Lebanon'; Mahanaim is 'the two camps' with a note at 6:13

harden / hardening (σκληρύνω of Pharaoh, 9:18; πωρόω and πώρωσις of Israel, 11:7, 25, the callus word, as in Mark 3:5; John 12:40); a note at the first use in each place names the Greek word; topic hardening-of-heart
push away (God did not 'push his people away', the verb of the Septuagint of Psalm 94:14); a note at 11:1
remnant (gloss: 'the small group left over after a disaster'; topic remnant)
make jealous / stir to jealousy (from Deuteronomy 32:21; note at 10:19 and 11:11)
mystery (gloss: 'a secret of God, now revealed'; the Greek word is a hidden plan made known, not a puzzle)
endurance (active staying power under pressure) / trouble (pressure; 'trouble' or 'troubles'; 'distress' only for στενοχωρία) / tested character
By no means! (the diatribe's refusal; a note at 6:2 on the style; never 'God forbid')
God's children (both; the Greek 'sons' of 8:14, 19 gets a note at 8:14 on the heirs' status, τέκνα 8:16-17, 21 'children'); υἱοθεσία 'adoption as children'
futility (the Septuagint's word for Hebrew hevel, 'vapor' in Ecclesiastes; a note at 8:20)
craving / crave (where the Tenth Word is quoted, to match Exodus 20:17 and Deuteronomy 5:21, where the site renders chamad 'crave'); 'desire(s)' elsewhere (6:12)
plead (for us); the Spirit and Christ both 'plead'
win an overwhelming victory (the single compound verb; not 'more than conquerors')
lord it over (the verb built on 'Lord')
as a sin offering (the Septuagint's phrase for hatta't; the note gives 'for sin' as the other reading)
firstfruits (as the Old Testament term, topic firstfruits)

God's righteousness (δικαιοσύνη 'righteousness', δικαιόω 'justify', as in content/terms.json); a gloss at first use and a note listing the readings (a gift God gives, God's own justice, his covenant faithfulness, his saving power); never 'justice' in the Plain; ἀδικία 'unrighteousness'

the place of atonement (Romans 3:25), with the gloss 'where sin is covered over' and a note on the readings (the atonement lid of the ark, propitiation, expiation, the martyrs' death of 4 Maccabees 17:22); Hebrews 9:5 'the atonement lid', the site's term for kapporet; topic atonement
redemption (gloss 'being set free by a price paid')
anger, with 'wrath' in the gloss at first use and the topic wrath; 'the day of anger' (2:5); θυμός 'fury' (2:8)
works of the law (literal), with a note giving the readings: boundary markers of Jewish identity (Dunn), the deeds the law requires (Moo, Cranfield), Luther's reading, and 4QMMT
reckon (an accounting word; one English word through chapter 4 so the reader can follow it); 'count' in 2:26; the gloss 'credit to the account' at 4:3
hand over / handed over (one English word in all five places, so the reader sees that God hands humanity over and hands the Son over); note at 1:24

brothers (as in Acts, which writes 'brothers' in the Plain), with a gloss 'brothers and sisters' and a note at 1:13 that the plural includes women; the Rom brief's 'brothers and sisters' was set aside to match Acts
nature / use (the natural use, 1:26-27, a Greek and Jewish idea of what is natural; note and gloss 'natural sexual relations' at 1:26)
conscience (one rendering at each; gloss 'the inner voice that judges right and wrong')
the obedience of faith (literal at both ends of the letter, with a note on the three readings: apposition, source, object)
the oracles of God (gloss 'God's spoken words'; note: the Scriptures or the promises)
transgression (stepping over a marked line) / trespass; ἁμαρτία stays 'sin', ἁμαρτάνω 'sin' (verb); ὑφ' ἁμαρτίαν 'under sin' with a note that Paul speaks of sin as a power

son of man (lowercase, every time, as in Psalm 8:4 and Revelation 1:13 'a son of man'); note at 2:1: God's usual way of addressing the prophet, a mortal set beside the glory above him; Greek huios anthropou. The Gospel title is handled by the topic son-of-man. Why: a reader following the phrase across the Bible has to see the same words.
the glory of the LORD (also 'the glory of the God of Israel', 8:4; 9:3; 10:19; 11:22; 43:2). Never 'weight' or 'honor' in the Plain; the root meaning 'heavy' goes in a note. Topic glory.
living creatures (chapter 1) = cherubim (10:1-22, as 10:15 and 10:20 say); topics living-creatures and cherubim; the ox of 1:10 is a 'cherub' in 10:14 (note there)
wheels (ofannim); galgal 'whirling wheel' (10:2, 6, 13) is a different word, with a note at 10:13
dome (never 'firmament', which comes from Latin firmamentum, Jerome's rendering of the Greek stereoma); note at first use. Genesis 1 uses the site's own word for raqia' there; the note points to it.

glowing metal (note at 1:4: the word is found only in Ezekiel; the Greek has elektron, 'amber' or an alloy of gold and silver; the KJV has 'amber'; Modern Hebrew chashmal 'electricity' was taken from this verse in the 1800s)
sapphire-like stone (the ancient sapphir was probably lapis lazuli, deep blue with gold flecks; note at first use)
the likeness of / something like / looking like: keep the careful chain of hedging in 1:26-28 and say so in a note at 1:5; never drop the hedges
rebellious house (one English every time; never 'house of rebels' or 'rebellious people'); meri alone 'rebellious'
watchman (for the prophet, and for the city's watchmen in 33:2); topic watchman

filthy idols (as in 1 Kings 15:12); note once in each part: the word is probably a mocking one, near gelel 'dung pellets' and galal 'roll'; the Greek has eidola. shiqqutsim 'detestable things' and to'evot 'abhorrent things' are different words and are kept apart. Why: the three are listed together in 5:11 and 7:20; blending them hides that Ezekiel names three words for one failing. Leviticus 26:30 (the same word) reads 'idols' on this site; the Ezekiel notes say so at 6:4.

yad'u ki ani YHWH (the recognition formula, Ezekiel: counted in the Hebrew, 56 verses have a form of 'know' directly followed by 'that I am the LORD' and five more 'that I am the Lord GOD', 61 in all)

Then they will know that I am the LORD (and 'you will know' when the Hebrew is second person); one fixed sentence every time. Where the Hebrew says 'that I, the LORD, have spoken' (5:13, 15, 17; 17:21, 24; 21:17, 32; 22:14; 24:14; 26:14; 30:12; 34:24; 36:36; 37:14: checked in the Hebrew) the Plain says 'that I, the LORD, have spoken'; where a clause is added (7:9 'the one who strikes') it is added after the fixed sentence. Note at the first use; the pattern gets a paragraph on the first chapter page.
the city of bloodshed; dam is 'blood' or 'bloodshed' by context
a mark (the letter tav; in Old Hebrew written like an X or +); note gives the church fathers (Origen, Tertullian, Jerome: the cross) and Rashi and Shabbat 55a

spirit, breath or wind by context. In 37:1-14 a single English word for the one Hebrew word wherever English allows, with the wordplay laid out in a note at 37:1. In 1:12, 20 and 2:2 'spirit' with a note that it can be 'wind'. 36:26-27 shows 'new spirit' and 'my Spirit' as the same word.
the uncircumcised (of the dead in Sheol), with a note on what the word meant to Ezekiel's hearers
the Pit (capitalized, as in Isaiah 14:15); Sheol stays Sheol
the sons of Zadok (the Levite priests of Zadok's line); topic zadok
the people of the land (one English every time; note at first use that who is meant differs by passage)

the chief leader of Meshech and Tubal (MT, rosh as 'chief'), with a note and a variant for 'the leader of Rosh, Meshech and Tubal'; Gog of the land of Magog. The Plain does not argue for or against any later identification.
Hamon-gog (the Valley of Hamon-gog, 'the horde of Gog'); Hamonah; the meaning in a gloss
The LORD Is There (the Hebrew in a gloss)
Daniel (spelled dn'l; the note on the Ugaritic king Danel of the Aqhat tale is a `com` note with its source)
bear the guilt (as in Leviticus 26:39 and Numbers 5:31); 'avon is 'guilt' (also the guilt-bearing 'wrongdoing'); chatta't is 'sin'. Why: matches the Leviticus choice.
rulings / rules (never 'statutes' or 'ordinances'); 'mishpat' in a courtroom sense 'judgment' by context (5:8)

plague (as in Leviticus 26:25; Jeremiah uses 'disease' for deber everywhere): Ezekiel's trio of sword, famine and plague (with the wild animals as a fourth in 14:21) keeps one word each Why (recorded exception): the Hebrew is the same word as Jeremiah's deber, which the Plain renders 'disease' in the stock triad 'sword, famine and disease' (about 25 verses) and which this site's Leviticus 26:25 renders 'plague'. Ezekiel follows Leviticus because 14:19 and 14:21 echo Leviticus 26 and the book sets the plague beside wild animals as a separate scourge. Unifying Jeremiah to 'plague' needs a Plain change across Jeremiah and is held in proposals/prophets/leftover.md.
the staff of bread (as in Leviticus 26:26; a note: the loaf as the staff a person leans on)

those who have insight / the insightful (the people with insight; gloss 'the teachers who understand God's plan'); the verb sakal 'give insight' in Daniel 9:22 is 'give insight'. Why: the same root joins 11:33-35 to 12:3, 10 and to Isaiah 52:13; 'the wise' (KJV, ESV, NIV) hides the link and clashes with chakham 'wise' elsewhere. Used in Daniel 11-12.
the regular offering (as Daniel 8:13). Exodus 29:38-42 and Numbers 28:3-8 describe the twice-daily lamb; 'daily offering' is Exodus's section heading, not its word for tamid.
a horror without end (Isaiah 66:24 'a horror to all flesh' is the only other use); cherpot 'shame'

change one's mind (about the harm planned), as in Jeremiah 26:3, 13, 19; 'I am tired of changing my mind' (15:6); note at first use in each part: the verb for God's changing course, see the topic gods-regret; the word ra'ah is 'harm' when the LORD plans it and 'wickedness' or 'evil' when people do it
falsehood (a lie when a person speaks it, 'lies' in the plural for speeches); the book's word for whatever cannot bear weight: 13:25; 14:14; 16:19
entice (the same English in both verses, so the link shows; note at 20:7 on 'deceive' and 'seduce')

sword, famine and disease (deber is 'disease' everywhere in Jeremiah: 14:12; 21:7, 9; 24:10; 27:8, 13; 29:17-18; 32:24, 36; 34:17; 38:2; 42:17, 22; 44:13) Why (recorded exception): deber is 'plague' in Ezekiel and Leviticus 26:25; Jeremiah's fixed triad reads 'disease' (the Greek has thanatos 'death'); see the Ezekiel entry for dever.

'ammi alone is 'my people' (6:14, 27); bat 'ammi, literally 'the daughter of my people', is 'my dear people' every time (4:11; 6:26; 8:11, 19, 21-22; 9:1, 7); betulat bat 'ammi (14:17) is 'the virgin, my dear people'. Why: the 'daughter' is the people seen as a loved young woman, not a second person. 6:14 and 8:11 are the same verse except for this word, and the Plain keeps the difference (notes at 6:14 and 8:11).

ruin (the loincloth, Judah's pride and the potter's vessel use one English verb) Not the same word as shachat 'slaughter' (Leviticus; sh-ch-t with tet, a different root from sh-ch-t with tav here, shachat 'ruin, spoil'); the two are spelled alike in English letters only. Lamentations' shever 'ruin' is another word again.

turn back (shuv) / turned away, turning away (meshuvah, shovav): 'Turn back, Israel, who turned away' (3:12); 'children who turn away' (3:14, 22); 'your turnings away' (2:19). Never 'backslide', 'repent' or 'faithless' for these in the text, so the play on turning stays visible; note at 3:12 in 01-06 (parts 07-12 and 26-31 follow, as 8:4-5 and 31:21-22 use the same root). Why: Jeremiah's key pun.

empty things / emptiness / become empty (the idols, 2:5); never 'vapor' (Ecclesiastes only) or 'vanity'; note at 2:5 in 01-06. The pun in 2:5 (walked after hevel and became hevel) is kept. Why (recorded exception): Ecclesiastes keeps 'vapor' for hevel as its one theme word (content/terms.json); in Jeremiah the word means the idols themselves ('empty things'), as in Deuteronomy 32:21 and Isaiah 'worthless idols' ('elilim, a different word).
the Shameful Thing (a name for Baal; capitalized; note at 3:24 in 01-06, with Ish-bosheth and Mephibosheth); in 11:13 'altars to the Shameful Thing'.

God when it names Israel's God ('elah, the God of heaven); the gods when a pagan speaks (2:11); 3:25 bar-'elahin 'a son of the gods' (note kind mis on the KJV 'the Son of God'); the Aramaic plural 'elahin qaddishin (4:8-9, 18; 5:11, 14) is 'a spirit of the holy gods' with a note that it can mean 'a holy god' (part 04-07)

the God of the heavens (note at 2:18), as in Ezra and Nehemiah (Ezra 5:11; 6:9; 7:12; Nehemiah 1:4). Why: the lead decided on the plural-form rendering for all the Aramaic and Hebrew uses of this title; the singular 'a God in heaven' at 2:28 (bishmayya) is a different form.
statue (the Aramaic is the word for 'image' in Genesis 1:26; note at 2:31). 'Image' stays in Genesis 1:26-27
segid: 'worship' of the statue (3:5-18, 28) and 'paid homage' to Daniel (2:46, the king's act); pelach: 'serve' of gods and of Israel's God (3:12, 14, 17, 18, 28)
achashdarpenayya / signaya / pachavata / adargazrayya / gedavrayya / detavraya / tiftaye (Daniel 3:2-3)
satraps / prefects / governors / advisers / treasurers / judges / magistrates (a fixed list; the sense of the last two is uncertain; note at 3:2); hadavrin (3:24, 27) 'counselors'
the king's rich food (a Persian loanword; note at 1:5)
secret (Persian loanword; Greek mysterion in both Greek forms; note at 2:18)
in the last days (as Genesis 49:1); note at 2:28 that the sense moves between 'later time' and 'the end'

How (the cry that opens a funeral song, as in Isaiah 1:21; 'eikh in 2 Samuel 1:19); the Hebrew title of the book, with a note at 1:1. Why: a question word 'How' keeps the dirge cry; 'Alas' is for hoy.
lament (the genre; 'dirge' in a gloss or note): a song of grief, usually with a longer line followed by a shorter one; the Talmud's name for Lamentations is Qinot
compassion(s) / women known for compassion (the root of 'womb'); the same root joins 3:22 to 4:10 and the Plain leaves the link visible
wait (both yachal and qavah) / in silence (dumam); darash 'look for'
man (in 3:1 'the man'); a strong man, not 'adam 'human being' or 'ish 'husband'; note at 3:1
festival (one English word each time; the LORD 'calls a festival' against the city in 1:15 and 2:22 invites terrors 'as for a festival day')
his footstool (the ark, the temple or Zion)
an unclean thing (the uncleanness of a woman's period; used of a city treated as unclean)
young women (plural) / the virgin, Daughter X (the personified title)
bat Yehudah / bat Yerushalayim / bat Edom (Lamentations 1:15; 2:2, 5, 13, 15; 4:21-22)
Daughter Judah / Daughter Jerusalem / Daughter Edom, as for Daughter Zion

anger / burning anger / rage / fury / indignation, one English word each. OPEN INCONSISTENCY (recorded at the merge, not hidden): this is the pairing in Ezekiel and Lamentations. Isaiah, Jeremiah and Daniel 9:16 render chemah 'fury' (for example Jeremiah 7:20, 'my anger and my fury'), so the same Hebrew word reads 'rage' in two books and 'fury' in three. A single rendering needs a Plain pass over Isaiah, Jeremiah, Daniel and Ezekiel with every note anchor re-checked; it is held in proposals/prophets/leftover.md for Matt to choose the direction (chemah 'fury' with 'evrah 'outburst', or chemah 'rage' with the older books changed).

sevens (seventy sevens, seven sevens, sixty-two sevens, one seven; gloss 'a seven, read as seven years in most readings'); never the KJV's 'weeks'. 10:2-3 shavu'im yamim is 'three weeks of days' (the Hebrew adds 'days' to mark ordinary weeks). Note at 9:24. Why: the Hebrew counts sevens without saying of what; the topic seventy-sevens lays out the readings.

an anointed one (not 'the Messiah', no capital, since the Hebrew has no article) / ruler (as nagid elsewhere); 'an anointed one, a ruler' (9:25); 'a ruler who is coming' (9:26). Note at 9:25 on who is meant.

the rebellion that desolates (8:13) / the abomination that desolates (11:31; 12:11); in 9:27 the plural 'abominations' and the person 'one who makes desolate' are kept as the Hebrew has them. pesha' is 'rebellion' everywhere (8:12-13; 9:24); shiqqutz is 'abomination'. The Greek of 1 Maccabees 1:54 and Mark 13:14 (bdelygma tes eremoseos) is 'the abomination of desolation', quoted only in notes. Why: the Hebrew phrase is a deliberate sound-play, and the Plain keeps the same two English words so the link shows; note at 9:27.

sanctuary (miqdash, 8:11; 9:17) / the holy place (qodesh, 8:13-14; 9:26) / a most holy place (qodesh qodashim, 9:24, as Exodus 26:33-34). Note at 9:24: the last could be a place, an altar or a person.

prince (sar ha-tsava 'the prince of the army', sar sarim 'prince of princes', the princes of Persia and Greece, 'one of the chief princes', 'your prince'); never 'commander' or 'archangel'; the same English each time so the angelic princes of chapter 10 can be seen with 8:11, 25 and 12:1. Notes at 8:11 and 10:13.
army: 'the army of the sky' (8:10, as 2 Kings 17:16; the stars and the angels), 'the army' (8:11-13); 'a great war' in 10:1, with a note that tsava can also mean hard service.
the time of the end (and 'the appointed time of the end', 8:19); note at 8:17: the end whose end is meant depends on the reading.

the Beautiful Land (as Ezekiel 20:6, 15, where the same word is said of the land; Jeremiah 3:19 has tsevi inside a longer phrase and reads 'an inheritance finer than that of any nation'); note at 8:9. Not the tsevi 'gazelle' of Song of Songs (content/terms.json): the Hebrew word is the same, and its two senses are 'gazelle' and 'beauty, splendor'; in Daniel the 'splendor' sense is certain from the phrase.
a highly treasured man (9:23 'you are highly treasured'); the same word in 10:3 is the 'fine food' Daniel gives up. Note at 9:23.
will be set right (a rare Niphal of tsdq; the Greek and Latin have 'cleansed'); note at 8:14.
Greece (the king of Greece, the prince of Greece); Javan is the name in Genesis 10:2; note at 8:21.

period / periods (4:16 'seven periods'); 7:25 'a time, times and half a time'. The Aramaic does not say how long a period was, so the Plain never says 'years' in chapter 4 (the Old Greek does). Why: a reader following 7:25 to Revelation 12:14 must see the same words.
watcher (always 'a watcher, a holy one'); note links the topic fallen-angels. Why: the word occurs only here in the Bible and is the Aramaic word behind the Watchers of 1 Enoch.
satraps / overseers / prefects / governors (Daniel 6); each fixed, glossed at first use as 'provincial governors', 'top administrators', 'high officials'.
the Ancient of Days (kept as a title); note: 'one advanced in days'; topic ancient-of-days.

the holy ones of the Most High; 7:27 'the people of the holy ones of the Most High'; gloss 'God's holy people or angels?'. Never 'saints' in Daniel (Revelation's term for hoi hagioi is a different word and a later use).

profane (to make what is holy common; note at first use in each part, with the gloss 'treated as common, not holy'). Leviticus on this site renders the same verb 'treat as common' (Leviticus 18:21; 20:3); Ezekiel keeps 'profane' because the profaning of the LORD's name is the book's central idea (20:9; 36:20-23). Why: one English word for the verb across the book, and the Leviticus rendering is cited in the note.

chamber (gate room) / porch / pillar / great hall (hekhal, as 1 Kings 6:3, 17); qodesh haqqodashim of the inner room 'the most holy place'. Why: matches the site's 1 Kings 6 (great hall, most holy place); one English per Hebrew word through Ezekiel 40-48.
the separate area / the building / room / side room; one English each across 40-48
cubit = 'a cubit and a handbreadth' (the long cubit, about 52 cm); the reed is six long cubits; glosses give metric figures
hearth (the altar's fireplace on top), with the Hebrew spelling and the Ketiv/Qere in the note at 43:15
consecrate ('fill the hand'), with the idiom in a gloss

contribution (a portion lifted off for the LORD, as in Leviticus 7:14); the land district is 'the holy contribution'. Why: matches Leviticus 7:14 and keeps one English for the word in the land and the grain passages.
charge (the guard duty over the holy things); one English every time in 44-48.
the year of release (the Jubilee, as Leviticus 25:10 'release'); note at first use.
foreigner(s) (uncircumcised outsiders in the sanctuary); distinct from the resident ger of 47:22-23, 'foreigners who live among you'.

1:9 'loyal love and compassion' (the site's hesed and rachamim terms); 2:18 Aramaic rachamin 'compassion'. Why: the review found 'favor' and 'mercy' did not match the site's terms; Daniel uses the common ones.

Jeremiah: crash (a great crash, crash after crash; an event), and 'the broken place' of the people in 6:14 and 8:11 where it is the wound; note at 4:6 in 01-06. Lamentations: ruin (the lasting state of a broken people); notes at 2:11 point to Jeremiah 6:14 and 8:11. Why (recorded exception): it is one Hebrew word; Jeremiah's 'crash' is a sudden break and Lamentations' 'ruin' is the state after it, and 'ruin' alone would blur Jeremiah's repeated 'crash after crash'. Held for review in proposals/prophets/leftover.md.

rebellion / sin / guilt / defy, one English word each and never swapped, in the Torah, Ezekiel, Lamentations and Daniel (marah 'defy' is the stubborn son's verb in Deuteronomy 21:18-20). Daniel 9 also has the verbs chata' 'sin', he'evinu 'gone wrong', hirsha'nu 'acted wickedly', marad 'rebel'; 9:5 keeps the three verbs of 1 Kings 8:47 in the same order. Why: the Torah (Exodus 34:7, Leviticus 16, Numbers 14:18) and Lamentations 4:22 and 5:7 render 'avon 'guilt'; Daniel 9:13, 16 and 24 first read 'wrongdoing' and were changed to 'guilt' at the merge so the one Hebrew word has one English word.

magicians / enchanters / sorcerers / the Chaldeans (a learned class; note at 1:4; shared term Kasdim) / diviners (gazrin are those who 'determine' fates, not 'astrologers') / wise men; one English word for each through the book (list notes at 1:20 and 4:7).

detestable thing(s) (Ezekiel 5:11; 7:20; 11:18, 21; 37:23; Jeremiah 4:1; 7:30; 13:27; 16:18; 32:34), distinct from to'evah 'abhorrent thing' (shared term) and gillulim 'filthy idols'. EXCEPTION: in the fixed phrase shiqquts meshomem (Daniel 11:31; 12:11) and in kenaf shiqqutsim (9:27), 'the abomination that desolates' and 'abominations', because 1 Maccabees 1:54 and Matthew 24:15 and Mark 13:14 quote it as 'the abomination of desolation' and a reader must see the link. The English word 'abomination' is never used for to'evah (Jeremiah 2:7 was changed to 'an abhorrent thing' at the merge) or for gillulim.

cypress (a tall evergreen: cypress, juniper or fir; the Isaiah 14:8 note at first use). Why: Isaiah 14:8 first read 'firs' while the rest of Isaiah and Ezekiel read 'cypress'; changed at the merge so the one Hebrew word has one English word.
royal power, as Psalm 22:28 has it; "the kingship" is the alternative
rescuers, as for the judges in Judges 3:9, 15 and Nehemiah 9:27; the note gives the Greek 'those who are saved'
a huge fish (never 'whale'); in Jonah 2 'the fish'. The Greek ketos is 'sea monster' where Matthew 12:40 has it. Note at Jonah 1:17.
a leafy plant (castor-oil plant? gourd? ivy?); the variant at 4:6 lists the Hebrew, the Greek kolokynthe 'gourd' and Jerome's hedera 'ivy'
appointed, every time, so the four appointments (fish, plant, worm, east wind) stay visible

change his mind (about the harm), the same English as Jeremiah 18:8-10; 26:3, 13, 19 and Joel 2:13-14, so Jonah 4:2 matches Joel 2:13 word for word ('slow to anger and great in loyal love, ... changes his mind about the harm'). Why: the brief's 'relent' was set aside to follow the Jeremiah Plain, as brief-twelve told the writer to do.

wickedness (1:2), evil (3:8, 10 the Ninevites' 'evil way'; 4:1 'a great evil to Jonah'), disaster (1:7-8, the storm), harm (3:10; 4:2, what the LORD planned, as in Jeremiah), misery (4:6); each note at first use shows the link
hurl / go down, one English word each across the book so the repetition is visible
a Hebrew (the foreigners' word for an Israelite; the Greek has 'servant of the Lord', in the variant at 1:9)
sheep breeder (note at Amos 1:1: a rare title, perhaps an owner or manager of flocks; the Greek writes it as a name)
herdsman / one who tends sycamore figs (the verbless clause rendered in the present, "I am no prophet"; note gives the past reading)
al shelosha pish'e X ve-al arba'a (Amos 1:3-2:6)
For three rebellions of X, and for four (pesha' is always "rebellion"); lo ashivenu is "I will not turn it back", with the object left open as in the Hebrew
the cutting locust (the first of the four locust words of Joel 1:4; Amos 7:1 gobai is "a swarm of locusts")

changed his mind about this: follows Exodus 32:14 and Jeremiah 18:8 in the site Plain, not "relent"; Joel 2:13-14 and Jonah 3:9-10 should match. Why: the brief proposed "relent" but the existing Plain uses "change his mind" everywhere for this verb.
a stream that never runs dry (as in Deuteronomy 21:4); nachal alone is "wadi" (Amos 6:14)

the cutting locust / the swarming locust / the hopping locust / the stripping locust: four English words kept apart in both verses (the Greek likewise keeps four names). 'Arbeh alone elsewhere is 'locust' or 'locusts' (Exodus 10); Amos 7:1 and Nahum 3:15-17 use other words. Why: the four names must stay visible; the notes at Joel 1:4 give the stage, kind, name and empire readings.
qiddesh (a fast, an assembly, war; Joel 1:14; 2:15-16; 3:9)

consecrate (a fast; the congregation; war), as Jeremiah 6:4 and 51:27 have 'consecrate war'; a gloss at each use says 'set apart as holy'. Why: one English verb for one Hebrew verb across Joel and Jeremiah.
sacred assembly (as Isaiah 1:13); the 'atseret of Leviticus 23:36 and Deuteronomy 16:8 stays 'closing assembly'.

the early rain to set things right (tsedaqah 'what is right' by context); the note and variant give 'the teacher of righteousness' (Vulgate) and the Greek 'food for righteousness'. The Qumran title is a separate matter.
the northern one (singular, as the Hebrew has it); the note gives the locust, human army and end-time readings.
the valley of decision; the note gives 'threshing sledge' (Isaiah 28:27; 41:15) as the other sense of charuts.
turn the fortunes ... around, as Jeremiah 29:14; 30:3; 33:7; the note gives 'captives' as the other sense.
'my Spirit' (capital S for the LORD's own) and 'all flesh', as Acts 2:17-18 has 'my Spirit' and 'all flesh'; the note on 2:28 gives the Hebrew.
the Greeks (literally 'the sons of the Ionians'); Daniel's Yavan is 'Greece', Genesis 10:2 'Javan'.
gives out his voice (Amos 1:2 has the same Hebrew and must match)
sweet wine (Amos 9:13 has the same Hebrew and must match)

changes his mind about the harm, following the Jeremiah entry (Jeremiah 18:8; 26:3, 13). The brief for the Twelve proposed 'relent'; Joel follows the existing entry, and Jonah 3:10 and 4:2 and Amos 7:3, 6 should be aligned to whichever the lead chooses.

prostitute oneself / prostitution, every time (never 'adultery' or 'unfaithfulness', which would decide what Gomer was); na'af is 'commit adultery' and is kept apart; the note at Hosea 1:2 gives the debate on sacred prostitution
knowledge of God, every time; yada' 'know' (2:20; 5:3-4; 6:3) is 'know', and the note at Hosea 2:20 gives the sense of relationship. Topic knowledge-of-god.
Jezreel / Lo-ruhamah / Lo-ammi, kept as names with a gloss at first use ('God sows'; 'Not Shown Compassion'; 'Not My People'); the cancelled forms are 'Ammi' and 'Ruhamah' in 2:1.
bring a case against / a case against (the covenant lawsuit), as Micah 6:1-2 and Isaiah 1:2 in the Plain; the note at Hosea 2:2 gives the form.
shrine woman / shrine women, as Deuteronomy 23:17 in the site Plain; Genesis 38:21 has 'holy woman'. Not 'cult prostitute' (the note gives the debate).
lovers (the Baals and the nations at once), one English word each time
Israel's pride (the note gives 'the Pride of Israel' as a possible divine title)

idol priests (the priests of false gods; note at first use in each book: the word is found only in these three places and is related to Akkadian and Syriac words for priest). Why: matches the Plain of 2 Kings 23:5 and Hosea 10:5.

the army of the heavens (the sun, moon and stars worshiped as gods). OPEN INCONSISTENCY: Deuteronomy 4:19, 2 Kings 17:16 and Daniel 8:10 read 'army of the sky'; Zephaniah follows 2 Kings 23 and Jeremiah, where the Hebrew is the same.
humble ('anavim, 2:3) / afflicted ('ani, 3:12) / poor (dal, 3:12), kept apart; note at 2:3 on the anawim; topic anawim.
pure lips (safah 'lip' is also 'language', as in Genesis 11:1; the note at 3:9 gives the readings: cleansed speech, one speech, restored Hebrew).
bring punishment on (the verb also means 'attend to', 2:7; 'enroll' in a census; the context decides).
the Second District / the Mortar (districts of Jerusalem; the market).
plan (1:10; 3:9, 'the plan of the mystery'); 'the task of managing' where Paul's own assignment is meant (3:2); a note at 1:10 gives the household-manager root and ties the three uses together
bring together (Ephesians 1:10, 'bring all things together in Christ'); 'sum up' in Romans 13:9; topic recapitulation
the heavenly world (never 'heavenly realms' or 'heavenly places'; the Greek is the neuter plural 'the heavenly things'); a note at 1:3
ruler, authority, power, lordship (ἀρχαί 'rulers' and ἐξουσίαι 'authorities' in 1:21, 3:10 and 6:12; ἀρχή 'beginning' elsewhere); topic spiritual-powers; κοσμοκράτορες (6:12) is the second part's

down payment (a first installment that guarantees the rest); gloss at Ephesians 1:14; a note at 2 Corinthians 1:22 lists the other English choices (pledge, guarantee, deposit) and Genesis 38:17-20 in the Greek. Why: one Greek word gets one English word in all three places, and "down payment" says both that the Spirit is given now and that more is to come
seal ('you were sealed'), with a gloss 'stamped as God's own'
fullness (one English word in all five places); note at 1:23 on the readings
the inner self (as Romans 7:22), with a note at Ephesians 3:16
new humanity (Ephesians 2:15, 'one new humanity', because the Greek ἄνθρωπος means a human being, not a male); 4:24 'the new self' is the second part's
the middle wall, the wall that fenced us apart; topic dividing-wall
the commonwealth of Israel (gloss: Israel's community of citizens); note on 'citizenship' and 'way of life' (Acts 22:28; 2 Maccabees 8:17)
resident alien / stranger (πάροικος a foreigner living in a city without citizens' rights; ξένος a stranger); topic foreigners
access (the noun); Romans 5:2 renders the same root with the verb 'led in', so a note at Ephesians 2:18 joins them
mystery (as Romans 11:25; 16:25), with a gloss 'a secret of God, now told' at 1:9; the Latin sacramentum in a note at 5:32 (second part)
without God (a note: the Greek is the origin of 'atheist' but means without the God of Israel)
cornerstone (note on the capstone reading); topic cornerstone

the basic elements of the world (4:3); 'those weak and poor elements' (4:9). A note at 4:3 lists the five readings. The family στοιχέω 'fall in line' (Galatians 5:25) and συστοιχέω 'line up with' (4:25) keeps the root visible. Topic elements-of-the-world.
ἔργα τῆς σαρκός / ὁ καρπὸς τοῦ πνεύματος (Galatians 5:19-23)

the works of the flesh / the Spirit's fruit (plural 'works', singular 'fruit', kept apart); the nine are love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness, self-control (πίστις is 'faithfulness' in this list only, with a note). Topic fruit-of-the-spirit.
the law of Christ (literal; a note gives five readings); ἔννομος Χριστοῦ (1 Corinthians 9:21) is 'under Christ's law'. Topic law-of-christ.
the Israel of God (literal; a note on the grammar of kai and the readings: the church, Jewish believers, the Jewish people; topic church-israel).
marks (the marks of Jesus); a note on brands, scars and the later 'stigmata'.
being said as an allegory (the only New Testament use; the note separates allegory, typology and midrash).
disturb / throw into turmoil (the agitators: 'the one who is disturbing you' 5:10, 'throwing you into turmoil' 5:12). Galatians 1:7 should read 'disturbing' to match, if the 01-03 writer agrees.
ἀσέλγεια / κῶμος / μέθη / ἔρις / ζῆλος (Galatians 5:19-21; Romans 13:13)
shameless living / wild parties / drunkenness / fighting / jealousy (the same English as Romans 13:13 where the Greek is the same).

comfort / comfort (1:3–7; 7:6–7, 13), one root kept visible; where Paul appeals the Plain says 'urge', 'beg' or 'appeal' (2:8; 5:20; 6:1; 8:6; 10:1; 13:11), with a note at 1:3 that it is one Greek word group; the Advocate (John 14:16) is the same root

set aside (passive: 'was being set aside', 'is being set aside'); one rendering in all four places, neutral between fade, end and lose power. Why: 'passing away' chose the fading reading and made 3:14 sound like a slow process; the note at 3:7 sets out the options. The 'passed away' of 2 Corinthians 5:17 is a different verb (parerchomai). Elsewhere in Paul (Romans 3:31; 6:6; 1 Corinthians 15:24, 26) the context decides
lead in a victory parade (the Roman triumph); the Plain keeps 'victory parade' so that the readings captive, soldier and instrument stay open; note at 2:14

reconcile / reconciliation, as in Romans 5:10–11; God is the one who acts; ἀποκαταλλάσσω (Colossians 1:20, 22; Ephesians 2:16) is the related compound, 'reconcile' too; topic ministry-of-reconciliation
ministry (the serving work, with a gloss 'serving work' on request); διάκονος 'servant' as in the existing entry, and δοῦλος 'slave' kept apart (4:5)

the letter / the Spirit; 'the letter' is kept literal with a note listing the readings (the literal sense, the Law without grace, the condemning Law, the Sinai covenant, a contrast with Paul's rivals); topic law-of-moses
be an ambassador / ambassadors (the emperor's and the kings' envoys); note at 2 Corinthians 5:20
ἡ ἐπιστολὴ ἡμῶν / συστατικαὶ ἐπιστολαί (2 Corinthians 3:1–3)
letters of introduction ('letters of recommendation' in the note), and 'our letter' for the church itself; Plain 'vouch for ourselves' for συνιστάνειν (3:1; 5:12) in the sense of recommend

offering (not 'grain offering'). WHY: in Malachi minchah covers animal and grain gifts alike (1:13 the lame animals; 2:12; 3:3-4), as in Genesis 4:3-5 and 1 Samuel 2:17, so the wide word is used throughout the book; zevach stays 'sacrifice'. The Hebrew is the same word Leviticus 2 and Joel and Amos (and Daniel 9:21) render 'grain offering'; the note at 1:10 says so and at 1:11 gives the incense-and-offering pair. Lead-approved for Malachi only; other books keep 'grain offering'.
betray (Malachi 2:10-16, five times; Jeremiah 3:20; 12:6); one English each time so the repetition shows

poor (not 'humble' or 'gentle'): the king of 9:9 and 'the poor of the flock' (11:7, 11) are the same Hebrew word, as in Zephaniah 3:12 'afflicted and poor'. Note at 9:9 on Matthew 21:5's 'gentle' (Greek praus).
Favor / Union (the names of the two staffs); notes give 'Beauty' and 'Bonds' as other renderings and the Septuagint's Kallos and Schoinisma.
pierce, pierce through: one English both times so the echo shows, and so John 19:37 and Revelation 1:7 'pierced' read as the same word.
the Feast of Booths (as Leviticus 23:34 and Deuteronomy 16:13 in the site Plain), not 'Tabernacles'.

Branch (capital B when it is a name or title: 'my servant, the Branch'; 'a man whose name is Branch'; Jeremiah 23:5 'a righteous Branch'). yitsmach (Zechariah 6:12) 'he will branch out', keeping the pun. Isaiah 4:2 'the LORD's branch' stays lower case (a different phrase and sense). The Greek anatole 'dawn, rising' gets its own note (Luke 1:78). Why: the brief fixed 'the Branch'; the topic branch already uses it.

the angel who spoke with me (the same English in every vision; the Hebrew bet is literally 'in', and the Greek has 'in me'; note at 1:9). The prophet's formula 'I looked up and saw' (va'essa 'einai va'ere: 1:18; 2:1; 5:1, 9; 6:1) is likewise fixed.

truth ('true justice' mishpat emet 7:9; 'the City of Truth' 8:3; 'in truth and in righteousness' 8:8; 'speak truth' 8:16; 'love truth and peace' 8:19). Why: one English word for the key word of chapters 7-8; 'faithfulness' stays for 'emunah.

did not change my mind (the same English as Jeremiah 4:28 and 18:8 in the site Plain); the piel noun and verb of the same root, 'comforting words' (1:13), 'comfort Zion' (1:17), are 'comfort'. The note at 8:14 shows that the root is one. Why: follows the 2026-10-28 lead decision for the Twelve.

'my Spirit' / 'his Spirit' with a capital S where the LORD speaks of his own Spirit (4:6; 7:12); 6:8 'my spirit' in lower case, with a note that the Hebrew can be anger (the Greek has thymos 'anger') or the Spirit.
the high priest (literally 'the great priest'); Joshua son of Jehozadak, as in Haggai (the same man as Jeshua son of Jozadak in Ezra and Nehemiah; note at 3:1).

appearing (of Christ Jesus: 'the appearing of our Lord Jesus Christ'), with a gloss at first use in each book ('his coming into view, as a god or a king shows himself'); the verb ἐπιφαίνω (Titus 2:11; 3:4) 'appeared'. The Maccabees entry 'appearance' (God's interventions) stays for 2 Maccabees. Why: one English word for the Pastorals' key word, kept apart from parousia 'coming'
εὐσέβεια / εὐσεβέω / εὐσεβῶς (1 Timothy 2:2; 3:16; 4:7-8; 5:4; 6:3-11; 2 Timothy 3:5, 12; Titus 1:1; 2:12)

godliness / show godliness (to) / in a godly way, with a gloss at first use in each book ('reverence for God lived out'; the word was also the everyday Greek virtue of piety toward gods, family and city); ἀσέβεια 'ungodliness' and ἀσεβής 'ungodly' (1 Timothy 1:9) as in the Wisdom and Maccabees entries; θεοσέβεια (1 Timothy 2:10) is a different word and is kept apart: 'honor God' (Plain of 1 Timothy 2:10)
πιστὸς ὁ λόγος (1 Timothy 1:15; 3:1; 4:9; 2 Timothy 2:11; Titus 3:8)

This saying is trustworthy (word for word in all five places; 'and deserves full acceptance' where πάσης ἀποδοχῆς ἄξιος follows, 1 Timothy 1:15; 4:9); a note at first use in each book on whether it points to the words before or after it
παρουσία, of Christ (1 Thessalonians 2:19; 3:13; 4:15; 5:23; 2 Thessalonians 2:1, 8; 1 Corinthians 15:23; Matthew 24:3, 27, 37, 39)

coming ('at his coming', 'the coming of our Lord Jesus'), with a gloss at first use in each book ('arrival, a royal visit'); of people, 'arrival' or 'presence' by context. Kept apart from ἐπιφάνεια 'appearing' and from εἴσοδος 'coming' in the sense of a visit (1 Thessalonians 1:9; 2:1). Lead decision of brief-pauline2.md; entry added by the 1Th writer
caught up ('will be caught up'), with a gloss naming the Latin rapiemur, the source of 'rapture'; elsewhere 'snatch (up/away)' as Acts 8:39, 2 Corinthians 12:2 and Revelation 12:5 already have it
to meet ('to meet the Lord in the air'), with a note on the civic welcome of an arriving ruler and the readings (escort back to earth, or taken to be with the Lord)

fall asleep / those who have fallen asleep (the image kept, as in 1 Corinthians 15), with a note at first use in each book that it is a common picture for death and does not by itself settle the state of the dead
anger, as the Romans entry: 'the anger that is coming' (1:10), with 'wrath' in the gloss
the rebellion (a revolt against God, as in the Greek of Joshua 22:22 and 1 Maccabees 2:15; Acts 21:21 'desert Moses' is the same noun); a note gives the minority 'departure' (rapture) reading
ὁ ἄνθρωπος τῆς ἀνομίας / ὁ ἄνομος / τὸ μυστήριον τῆς ἀνομίας (2 Thessalonians 2:3, 7, 8)
the man of lawlessness / the lawless one / the mystery of lawlessness (variant 'the man of sin' in the Byzantine text and KJV, given in variants.json)
ὁ υἱὸς τῆς ἀπωλείας (2 Thessalonians 2:3; John 17:12)

the son of ruin (as John 17:12 on this site); ἀπώλεια 'ruin', οἱ ἀπολλύμενοι 'those on the road to ruin' (2 Thessalonians 2:10). ὄλεθρος is also 'ruin' (see its entry); a note at 2 Thessalonians 1:9 says the two Greek words differ
what is holding him back / the one who is holding him back (neuter, then masculine; 'restrainer' only in notes)

out of line (a military word, 'out of rank'; one English phrase in all places so the reader can follow it; a note gives 'idle' and 'unruly'). 1 Thessalonians 5:14 should match if the 1Th writer agrees
tradition / traditions (the apostles' teaching handed on; Mark 7:8 'a tradition made by humans' uses the same word)

God-breathed (the only use in the Bible), with a gloss 'inspired by God, breathed out by him' and a note on the two ways to read πᾶσα γραφὴ θεόπνευστος καὶ ὠφέλιμος ('Every Scripture is God-breathed and useful' in the Plain; 'every God-breathed Scripture is also useful' in the note); topic inspiration-of-scripture
παραθήκη (1 Timothy 6:20; 2 Timothy 1:12, 14); verb παρατίθημι (2 Timothy 2:2)

deposit ('my deposit' 2 Timothy 1:12, left open between what Paul entrusted to God and what God entrusted to Paul; 'the good deposit' 1:14), with a gloss 'what was put into safekeeping'; the verb in 2 Timothy 2:2 is "entrust", to keep the link with the deposit
μορφή / σχῆμα / ὁμοίωμα (Philippians 2:6-8); σύμμορφος, συμμορφίζω, μετασχηματίζω (Philippians 3:10, 21; Romans 8:29)

form ('being in the form of God', 'taking a slave's form') / outward shape ('found in outward shape as a human being') / likeness ('the likeness of human beings'); the compounds keep the root visible: 'taking on the form of his death' (3:10), 'refashion ... to share the form of his body of glory' (3:21). No gloss at Philippians 2:6, so as not to choose among the readings; the note there gives them (divine nature, glory or majesty, status, Adam's image). Mark 16:12 'a different form'.
ἁρπαγμός (Philippians 2:6, the only New Testament use)

something to exploit ('he did not count equality with God / as something to exploit'; 'count' for ἡγέομαι as in 3:7-8), following the idiom reading of R. W. Hoover (1971); the note at 2:6 gives 'robbery' (KJV, active sense), a prize to be seized (res rapienda) and a prize held onto (res retinenda), and O'Neill's reply

empty ('he emptied himself', Philippians 2:7, literal, never 'made himself nothing' or 'of no reputation'); 'emptied' / 'made empty' in Romans 4:14 and 1 Corinthians 1:17 as already published; topic kenosis; the note at Philippians 2:7 says Paul names how (by taking a slave's form), not what was given up; no gloss on 'emptied himself', so as not to choose what was given up

ruin; ὄλεθρος αἰώνιος 'eternal ruin' (2 Thessalonians 1:9). Lead decision 2026-10-29: one word across Paul, so that 1:9 does not lean toward one reading of the judgment; the 2 Thessalonians note says it is a different Greek word from ἀπώλεια
working ('Satan's working', 'a working that leads them astray'): one rendering in both verses so the link the Greek makes stays visible; δύναμις is 'power'
